claims.text: The proposed high-entropy alloy has a complex multielement composition.
The proposed alloy inherently provides mechanical strength and wear resistance.
The proposed alloy has a baseline passive film that provides corrosion protection.
The coupled tribocorrosion response is governed by a dynamic balance between mechanical removal of the passive film and electrochemical stabilization or destabilization of its reformation.
Mechanical sliding disrupts and erodes the passive oxide film during tribocorrosion.
Applied electrochemical potential can directly control passive-film integrity during simultaneous wear.
A potential favoring passivity enhances reformation of the mechanically disrupted film.
A stable passive or protective oxide film reduces electrochemical corrosion attack.
Stabilizing the passive film reduces mechanical degradation and wear.
A destabilizing potential exacerbates passive-film removal.
At a film-stabilizing potential, both corrosion rate and wear rate will decrease relative to the baseline.
At a film-destabilizing potential, both corrosion rate and wear rate will increase relative to the baseline.
The potential-induced changes in degradation should be notable under aggressive corrosive conditions.
The controlled comparison varies electrochemical potential while holding the alloy samples, electrolyte, and mechanical sliding conditions constant.
The predicted trends may fail if the alloy cannot form a coherent passive film.
The predicted trends may fail if mechanical effects overwhelmingly dominate total degradation.
Failure to obtain systematic, reproducible decreases at stabilizing potentials and increases at destabilizing potentials would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as both a neutral electrochemical potential with no external modulation and a control tested under a specified neutral potential. It is unclear whether this means open-circuit conditions or an externally imposed potential.
